events.description: Uncover Music presents Caoilfhionn Rose Raised in Manchester, Caoilfhionn developed a "deep, almost spiritual appreciation" of music in all its diversity from a young age. Drawing inspiration from nature, dreams, and personal experiences, she crafts songs that are both intimate and universal in their themes. Inspired to begin writing and performing as well as studying music, Caoilfhionn started playing open mic nights around Manchester around 2013, while simultaneously embarking on a collaboration with The Durutti Column, one of Factory Records' most distinctive and prolific artists- an experience which, she says, "really helped open my mind and music world". A performance at a local café caught the attention of Gondwana Records founder Matthew Halsall, who invited Caoilfhionn to work on her debut album 2018's Awaken. It became the first of three albums for the label; followed by 2021's Truly and 2024's Constellation. As a bandleader she headlined tours across the UK and Europe and has also supported artists such as Mammal Hands, The Breath, GoGo Penguin, Alabaster dePlume and Hania Rani.

Uncover Music presents M/X M/X is a young and eclectic three-piece dream punk powerhouse that fuses post punk with grunge and indie gaze. Chaotically charming, their live shows consist of nothing but raw energy and zest. Hailing from Bristol, England, the band's visceral sound draws comparisons to the likes of IDLES, Yard Act, Talking Heads, Gurriers and Shame. With trashy rhythms, angsty guitars and socially charged lyrics that hit like a punch in the gut, their explosive performances have landed them spots at festivals like 2000 Trees and Dot To Dot, as well as conquering venues in Europe, including SuperSonic, Paris. With relentless drive and a DIY ethos, M/X started the year off strong by making their European live debut in February and they are gearing up for a huge 2026. Their debut EP is a visceral soundtrack to the chaos of modern life, offering a cathartic release in a world that rarely pauses to breathe. Followed by the single release of 'Momma' which is a dirty grunge anthem. It's raw, emotional, and honest. Whether on stage or in the studio, M/X promises to keep pushing boundaries and riling up crowds wherever they go next.

ai.en: Funke and the Two Tone Baby play Sunflower Lounge, presented by Uncover Music.

events.description: Uncover Music presents Funke and the Two Tone Baby Funke and the Two Tone Baby is a truly unique artiste. Designing music on a machine of his own creation whilst playing a genre and sound that is totally his own. Jammed between off-kilter garage beats with a flash of hip-hop, and high energy alternative blues with a dose of funk, is a whirling blur of glitches, big drops and jump up choruses. It's Fatboy Slim meets The White Stripes via LCD Soundsystem and a smattering of IDLES to boot. No one is making music in this way or in this style, and those who know, know, and those who don't are surely missing out. In February 2027, Funke returns with his 5th studio album 'Greebling'. 'Greebling' is the process of adding detail to increase the appearance of complexity and this new iteration of Funke promises to be more detailed and more complex than ever before. With the new album featuring guest appearances from Beans on Toast and Samantics, and once again produced by Dutty Moonshine Big Band's production genius, 'Binge', Funke's 5th LP stands head and shoulders above anything he has done so far on his long and dedicated music career. The new record contains all the elements of blues, electronica and ferocity that Funke's been evolving for the last 15 years, but distils it further down with tighter production, a fuller embrace of dance music culture and an ever-growing arsenal of instruments and repertoire. Trading an acoustic guitar for an electric, this new direction cuts through…

events.description: Uncover Music presents Rowena Wise Rowena Wise is a Naarm/Melbourne-based singer-songwriter whose work balances beauty and mess with rare emotional precision, drawing from 60s folk storytelling while grounded in indie rock, garage pop and alt-folk. Raised in Margaret River, Western Australia, by a luthier father and a Chicago-born folk musician mother, Wise moved to Melbourne at 18 to forge her own path. Since debuting in 2018, she has amassed over 10 million streams, earned airplay across triple j, double j and Unearthed, and toured extensively across Australia, the UK, Europe, the USA and Canada, supporting artists including Holy Holy, Ball Park Music, Bernard Fanning and Paul Dempsey. Her 2024 debut album, Senseless Acts of Beauty, was praised by CLASH Magazine as "carefully etched indie folk" and shortlisted for the Australian Music Prize. Her highly anticipated sophomore album, Bad Things Feel Good*, a tender, point-blank meditation on transformation produced by Rob Muinos (Julia Jacklin, Didirri), is out August 7, 2026 via Beloved.

events.description: Uncover Music presents Dan Croll With over 100 million streams to date, British singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist (piano, trumpet, guitar, bass, drums, and organ among them) Dan Croll gained early recognition. Being named Songwriter of the Year by the Musicians' Benevolent Fund in 2011 while attending the Paul McCartney-founded Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts, he has since built a reputation for his nuanced songwriting and distinctive sound. Speaking of 'Try Try Try', Dan says, "Whenever I hit a wall with songwriting, the only thing that really works is stripping everything back. 'Try try try' came from one of those moments. events.description: RUTS DC present 50 years of RUTS Music (1977-2027) THE RUTS + special guests In 1977, The Ruts emerged from London with a sound unlike anybody else around them - the raw urgency of punk colliding with reggae, dub and rock, driven by formidable musicianship and a fierce sense of purpose. With Malcolm Owen, Paul Fox, Dave Ruffy and Segs Jennings, The Ruts created a body of music whose power has endured far beyond its original moment. After losing Malcolm Owen in 1980, the remaining members chose integrity over nostalgia by re-inventing themselves as Ruts DC, eventually losing Paul Fox in 2007. Ruts DC remain a living, evolving band to this day. But the time has come to celebrate the whole story. This tour is about taking the music that exploded out of a movement and bringing it onto a stage in 2027 with all its urgency and relevance intact. Music made across five decades - from the albums The Crack and Grin & Bear It, through Animal Now, Rhythm Collision, Music Must Destroy, and Counterculture? with the classic singles In A Rut. Babylon's Burning. Something That I Said. Jah War. Staring At The Rude Boys. West One (Shine On Me) and more. An AGMP Concerts presentation. Uncover Music presents Quivers Quivers have been making jangle-damaged, lyric-driven guitar pop long enough now for R.E.M. to slide into their DMs. Dream US label Merge signed the band for their third release, Oyster Cuts, and Quivers toured with indie stalwarts Superchunk, as well as by themselves, all over Australia, Europe and North America in 2024, stopping in Seattle to film a second KEXP studio performance. A hiatus followed as Sam took a break to become a dad and write songs for the upcoming next album while pushing a pram and pointing at birds and planes. This next chapter features a louder trio sound with new collaborators Shauna Boyle (Cable Ties, drums/singing) and Thomas Skalicky (Little Island, bass/singing). It starts with rolling announcements of more national and international touring, and a new 7" single out November 4 on Merge, featuring "Bottle The Nervous" and a cover of The Vulgar Boatmen's 1989 roadtrip-obsessed gem "Drive Somewhere".

Uncover Music presents William The Conqueror William The Conqueror, the critically acclaimed, shape-shifting trio from Cornwall, have quietly established themselves as one of the UK's most vital underground bands. Rooted in groove driven alt-rock and steeped in the storytelling traditions of folk and Americana, their sound is equal parts fuzz and finesse and has seen them tour with everyone from Bright Eyes to Nathaniel Ratliffe and Wilco, making records with Ethan Johns (Kings of Leon, Laura Marling) and Joseph Lorge (Phoebe Bridgers, Perfume Genius) along the way. Now several albums deep, and never content to stand still, William The Conqueror continue to evolve - a band shaped by the road, sharpened in the studio, and sustained by a stubborn belief in the redemptive power of a great song, well played. William The Conqueror's live performances have drawn wildly enthusiastic comparisons to Kings of Leon, Nirvana, Buffalo Tom and The Marshall Tucker Band. Latest album "Maverick Thinker" (Chrysalis Records) has been described as "a record of cuts and bruises, wrapped within bittersweet leftfield rock n roll tunes; short, sharp shots to the arm; fuzzy college rock with chops, one foot lingering menacingly over the distortion pedal." Recorded in LA at the infamous Sound City Studios, the trio rattled through the album's ten tunes at a breakneck speed - the energy and chaos nods to some of the US lo-fi greats and yet arrives at something innately British.
